title: Quote the cheapest fee among what the merchant offers

blocks.text: At checkout, the customer is shown the way of paying that costs the merchant least. Merchants choose what they offer: some switch off the wallet or the bank transfer, and some have signed a rate of their own that sales loads from the contract. Support has two tickets: a merchant without bank transfers whose customers are told to pay by bank transfer, and a merchant whose negotiated card rate is never offered even though it is the cheapest.

items: `cheapest(offered, amountCents)`: the rule with the lowest fee for that amount, out of the rules this merchant offers.

blocks.text: When you're done, checkout picks among exactly what the merchant offers, standard method or negotiated rate. About five lines in total.

cases.says: with every standard method offered, the cheapest one for the amount is picked
the same methods offered in another order give the same answer
a standard method the merchant doesn't offer is never picked, even when it would be cheapest
a negotiated rate, which is not one of the enum's constants, is picked when it is the cheapest offered

origin.section: Callers Take an Interface the Enum Implements, So a Rule From Elsewhere Fits Too

concepts: An enum implementing an interface lets callers that take the interface accept rules that are not constants, such as negotiated rates or test stubs.
